newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 12.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Supertyphoon Dale spares the Philippines and veers away to southern Japan, forecasters at the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration said. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- Foreigners who join protest rallies during the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation summit face arrest and deportation, the Bureau of Immigration warns. (PHILIPPINE STAR)

- Superstar Michael Jackson is scheduled to call on Philippine President Fidel Ramos when he arrives for the History concert in December, presidential management staff chief Alexander Aguirre said. (MANILA TIMES)
- The presidential palace orders Governor Nur Misuari of the Autonomous Region of Moslem Mindanao to stop the rash of kidnappings in areas under his jurisdiction. (PHILIPPINE STAR)

- Leaders of both Houses of Congress have knocked off the income tax component of the Comprehensive Tax Reform Package and the retail trade liberalisation measures from their common legislative agenda for this current session. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- The Philippine government has rebuffed a proposal of the U.S. Trade Representative to raise the country's garments quota to settle a dispute over the new rules of origin (PHILIPPINE DAILY)
- Bayan Telecommunications Holdings Corp says it has acquired a 46.62 percent stake in beleaguered cellular phone operator Express Telecommunications Corp (TODAY)
